insights.topic: Verified purchase proof vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's protocol has cryptographically verified $4.93M in GMV across 103,038 receipts — each one a confirmed transaction, not an inferred intent signal. For brands paying $5+ CPM to reach people who might buy, this is a structurally different data asset: deterministic purchase proof at scale.

Pre-rolloff 7-day GMV peaked at ~$83.5K for two consecutive cycles, then stepped down to $75K in the most recent cycle — a ~10% drop that either reflects a throughput ceiling forming or a one-cycle compression anomaly. The 2026-11-13T20:15 reading is the diagnostic: if it recovers to ~$83.5K, the step-down was noise; if it holds below $80K, the platform has hit a near-term accumulation ceiling that limits audience scale claims.

insights.topic: Category mix stability — no distortion in the data
insights.insight: Category entropy has held at 2.905 bits across multiple consecutive snapshots, and the 14-day category breakdown shows proportional contraction across all five verticals — grocery, dining, retail, gas, and unknown — with no single category inflating or collapsing. For brands using this data for targeting or measurement, the mix is structurally stable and not an artifact of one vertical dominating.

insights.topic: Walmart, Kroger, Target concentration at the top
insights.insight: The three largest verified-receipt brands — Walmart (298), Kroger (132), and Target (124) — account for a disproportionate share of 14-day receipt volume, confirming this audience skews toward mass-market grocery and general merchandise shoppers. Brands in CPG, household goods, or adjacent retail categories are looking at a high-affinity audience; niche or premium brands should note the concentration before assuming broad reach.

insights.topic: Logistics receipts as a durable non-grocery signal
insights.insight: The UPS Store has re-entered the visible 14-day brand list at 43 receipts after multiple suppressed snapshots, confirming that shipping and logistics transactions are a structurally recurring category in this dataset — not a one-time anomaly. For brands targeting small business owners or active online shoppers, the presence of logistics receipts alongside grocery and retail is a meaningful behavioral signal.

insights.topic: Geographic coverage — pulse cells vs. durable metros
insights.insight: Of the 19 active CBSAs in the current snapshot, at least three are classified as recurring pulse cells — markets that appear intermittently rather than continuously, often correlated with UTC midnight rolloff windows. Brands planning geo-targeted campaigns against this data should distinguish between the durable core metros and these pulse markets before committing to local spend.
